funFact: Brazilian free-tailed bats can exit the cave in spiraling columns for up to 20 minutes.

description: Closer look at bats exiting the cavern.
funFact: These bats can fly over 100 miles in a single night to hunt insects.

description: Wide view of the largest cave chamber.
funFact: The Big Room is over 8 acres in size, making it one of the largest cave rooms in North America.

description: Detailed formations inside the Big Room.
funFact: The cave maintains a constant temperature of about 56°F year-round.

description: Looking down into the cave opening.
funFact: The natural entrance drops approximately 750 feet into the cavern system.

description: Winding path leading into the cavern.
funFact: Visitors descend over a mile of paved trail to reach the Big Room.

description: Wide opening of the cave from below.
funFact: The cave formed through sulfuric acid dissolving limestone rather than surface water erosion.
Cave formations can take hundreds of thousands of years to grow just a few feet.
Mineral colors come from iron, manganese, and other trace elements.

description: Original ladder used by early explorers.
funFact: Early explorer Jim White used homemade ladders in the early 1900s to enter the caverns.
The Big Room trail loop is approximately 1.25 miles long.
Electric lighting was installed in the 1930s to improve visitor access and safety.
Stalactites form from mineral-rich water dripping from the ceiling over long periods of time.

description: Narrow tunnel within the cave system.
funFact: Carlsbad Caverns National Park contains over 119 known caves.

description: Seating area for watching bat flights.
funFact: Rangers host nightly programs here during bat season to explain bat behavior and ecology.
